citation word read as 'nesem' with a short round s; could be 'necem' (lex si necem). The opening 'l' has no point after it, unlike the 'l.' of the other citations. The capital after it is clearly 'P.' (same sort as the 'P.' in note m), not 'D.'

the siglum opening this line is a long ſ followed by a short round s, with no point; it is certainly the Digest siglum usually printed 'ff.', but the glyph pair does NOT match the real 'ff' ligature of 'effract.' two notes below (two tall descending strokes with a shared crossbar), so it is transcribed as printed
the -que sign after 'itaq' is printed as a semicolon shape (dot over comma), not the 3-shaped ꝫ of §2; transcribed as ';'
